situation (example wording): "Compare murders in Washington, Baltimore, Charlotte, Jackson, Kansas City and Richmond" (city names in a question naming two or more places).
what the app does today: P28 offers Washington state beside Washington, D.C. and qualifying counties, and asks about a lone Charlotte with Charlotte, North Carolina and Charlotte County, Florida as choices under P28. P196 already resolves a city named beside other places to its city police without asking against its county, but does not settle Washington's state alternative.
proposed behavior: In a list of cities (two or more places named in one question), Washington means Washington, D.C., without the state or county choices P28 offers. Charlotte means Charlotte, North Carolina, alone or in a list, without offering Charlotte County, Florida. A lone "Charlotte" means Charlotte, North Carolina, no ask, an exception to P28's same-name ask. Baltimore, Jacksonville, St Louis and Los Angeles resolve to the city under P196. This does not remove P28's ask when two or more cities of the same name in different states each have at least 100,000 people: Kansas City (Missouri/Kansas) and Richmond (Virginia/California) still ask. Jackson means Jackson, Mississippi, under P28 because only that city of the name has at least 100,000 people. P196's rules stay as written, including its note naming the agency used where a county agency bears the same name. A single place on its own, including a lone "Washington", remains governed by P28, except Charlotte. An explicitly named state, county, county police department or sheriff's office retains its stated meaning. P28's state qualifier still narrows choices to that state. P70's countywide and metro rules and its note for a plain county name remain unchanged.
exact default or choices offered: For city names in a list, no county, sheriff or county police alternative is offered against the city (P196). Washington: Washington, D.C. Charlotte: Charlotte, North Carolina, alone or in a list, no ask. Jackson: Jackson, Mississippi. Kansas City without a state: ask with Kansas City, Missouri and Kansas City, Kansas. Richmond without a state: ask with Richmond, Virginia and Richmond, California.
why: Jeff 2026-11-22 (through the coordinator): Charlotte means Charlotte, North Carolina, with no ask; Washington named among a list of cities means Washington, D.C., with no ask. Kansas City and Richmond still ask under P28. Jeff also answered YES through the coordinator on 2026-11-22 that a lone "Charlotte" means Charlotte, North Carolina, with no ask, as an exception to P28's same-name ask.
